propositions: A provider-parity harness must measure whether the same logical requests produce identical payloads and tool availability across Anthropic and Bedrock providers, regardless of per-model non-determinism in decision outcomes.
Bedrock inference-profile ids are invokable in account 896586841071/us-east-1; both standard (claude-sonnet-4-6) and frontier (claude-opus-4-8) slots are measurable.

Payload parity and tool parity both hold across both class slots: system prompt, messages, max_tokens, and tools are byte-identical; only the model_id field differs (bare Claude vs us.anthropic prefixed); one legitimate capability difference (temperature=0.0 withdrawal on opus) is symmetric and model-driven not provider-driven.
Provider routing is clean: the Bedrock-configured arm makes zero non-Bedrock calls across measured case-runs, verified via per-call model tally from REBAR_USAGE_LOG.

The corpus selector must exclude non-agentic arms that bypass resolve_gate_config (completion-verifier, ticket-quality, spec-alignment) and pool 30 gold-labeled cases (15 block, 15 advisory) across 15 non-agentic specs to meet the MIN_GOLD_ITEMS=20 floor.

All observable decision-level flips between arms are genuine (error_rate=0.000 on both arms) and non-determinism between different models is expected and out of epic scope; payload/tool parity (not verdict parity) is the gate.
